clue.text: Setting including a large kind of triangle

indicators.note: a setting that includes something holds it inside itself, so the next words go within

parts.note: a scene is the setting of a play or story
taken as written
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A stage set that happens to feature a big triangle of some sort.
explanation.walkthrough: A and L go together inside SCENE to give SCALENE.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalene triangle is one whose three sides all differ in length, one of the named categories of triangle.

clue.text: Biblical character without fitting rank

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so the name surrounds the next word

parts.note: Cain, son of Adam and Eve, who killed his brother Abel
apt means suitable or fitting

explanation.surface: A figure from the Bible lacking the proper standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain is a grade of officer in the army and navy, so it is a military rank.

clue.text: Interior covering for passenger ship

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a lining fitted inside something, as in a bin bag or coat
second meaning: a large ocean-going vessel for travellers

explanation.surface: Choosing the decor for a cruise ship's cabins.
explanation.definitionFit: An inner protective layer is a liner, and so is a large ship on a regular ocean route.

clue.text: Eminent aristocrat entertaining volunteers

indicators.note: a host entertaining guests has them inside, so the peer holds the next group

parts.note: a noble is a member of the aristocracy
the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A distinguished lord hosting a party of part-time soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A notable person is prominent and distinguished, just as an eminent one is.

clue.text: A coat with line and wrinkles

parts.note: an animal's coat is its fur
a row is a line; the setter lets the phrase stand for rows

explanation.surface: Describing a lined coat that has become creased.
explanation.walkthrough: The S is loose: 'line' strictly gives ROW, so the setter treats 'with line' as rows of lining to make the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Furrows are deep lines or creases in the brow, so they are wrinkles in the face.

clue.text: Some tunes composed for an international organisation

indicators.note: some of the following words means only a run of letters from inside them is used

parts.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Music written for a global body such as the UN.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' looks like an anagram signal, but the letters sit in order inside the words.
explanation.definitionFit: UNESCO is the United Nations agency for education, science and culture, a body of many nations.

clue.text: Stand for religious education here

parts.note: RE is the British school subject Religious Education
someone here is present

explanation.surface: Advocating that religion be taught in this place.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent something is to symbolise it or act for it, which is what stand for means.

clue.text: Stitch up nurse in part of London

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: to stitch is to sew
to nurse a patient is to tend them

explanation.surface: A nurse being framed for a crime in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stitch up' reads as framing someone, but splits into stitch and up. The West End is London's central theatre and shopping district.
explanation.definitionFit: The West End is the area of central London known for theatres, shops and smart addresses.

clue.text: Grub garb

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the tough-skinned larva of the crane fly
second meaning: a coat made of hide

explanation.walkthrough: The two near-rhyming words look like one phrase; each takes a separate sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The crane fly's soil-dwelling larva has this name for its tough skin, and the same words name a coat made from hide.

clue.text: Frank is allowing access

definitions.meaning: first meaning: candid, honest and outspoken
second meaning: not shut, so people can get in

explanation.surface: Someone called Frank is letting people in.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a man's name, but it is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: An open person speaks candidly, and an open door or shop lets people enter.

clue.text: Playful pets after Lawrence takes them out to play

indicators.note: someone who takes people out on an outing goes among them, so the abbreviation sits inside that word

parts.note: taken as written
T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, is known by his initials

indicators.note: being playful means frisking about, so the letters of the next word romp into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Frisky pets taken out for a romp by a man named Lawrence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes them out' reads as walking the pets, but it means the initials go inside the word them; 'after' puts the rearranged pets last.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tempest is Shakespeare's late drama about Prospero on his island, so it is an example of a stage work.

clue.text: Sort of zebra crossing, good for capital city

indicators.note: something crossing a letter straddles it, holding it in the middle
a sort of something is a variant of it, so the letters of the animal come in a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
G is the usual abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A pedestrian zebra crossing that is handy for getting around a capital.
explanation.walkthrough: A zebra crossing is the British striped pedestrian crossing, which makes 'zebra crossing' read as one thing. Rearranged ZEBRA wraps G: ZAGREB.
explanation.definitionFit: Zagreb is the seat of government of Croatia, so it is a national capital.

clue.text: Given food in Australia, Edward is exhausted in America

parts.note: tucker is Australian slang for food
Ed is a short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: An Edward who was fed in Australia and then worn out in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a travelogue across two continents; each place tags a regional word, Australian slang for the wordplay and American usage for the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuckered, usually tuckered out, is American informal usage for being completely tired.

clue.text: Rental due to be revised is not revised

indicators.note: revising a text changes it around, so the two words before are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rent payment that is supposed to be reviewed, but the figure stays the same.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is the contradiction: the letters are revised to say they are not revised.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unaltered has had no changes made to it, which is exactly what remaining unrevised means.

clue.text: Ballerinas missing a dance in Wales

definitions.note: a phrase locating a place stands for the place itself, fair because the answer is simply somewhere found in Wales

indicators.note: letters that dance skip about into a new arrangement
missing means going without, so the single letter that follows is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
the letter to be dropped

explanation.surface: Dancers absent from a Welsh dance show.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one A from BALLERINAS and rearrange the rest. Llanberis is a village at the foot of Snowdon in North Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Llanberis is a village in Gwynedd, North Wales, so it is a place located there.

clue.text: Undergarment for a bear

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a one-piece woman's undergarment combining a chemise and knickers
second meaning: a child's soft toy bear

explanation.surface: Picture a bear being dressed in underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a one-piece lingerie item and the stuffed toy bear named after Theodore Roosevelt.

clue.text: Thatcher's choice for home secretary

definitions.meaning: first meaning: what a roof thatcher uses, dried stalks
second meaning: Jack ..., British Home Secretary from 1997 to 2001

explanation.surface: Margaret Thatcher picking a Home Secretary for her cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: Thatcher looks like the Prime Minister, but it is a person who thatches roofs. The Home Secretary is the UK minister for policing and immigration; Jack Straw held the post when this was set.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatchers roof cottages with dried stalks, and Jack Straw was the Labour minister running the Home Office.

clue.text: Instructor having meal with singer and actress

parts.note: tea is a light afternoon or evening meal in Britain
Cher is the American singer and actress

explanation.surface: A coach dining out with a celebrity performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher gives lessons, so the word is a straightforward synonym for an educator.

clue.text: Turning point when Tom Jones initially encounters flattery

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters, here of each of the two names

parts.note: the initial letters of the two names
unction is excessive, oily flattery or unctuousness

explanation.surface: The singer Tom Jones reaching a crisis when fans gush over him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning point' suggests a crisis, but is read literally: a place where the road turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-junction is where one road meets another at right angles, so drivers must turn there.

clue.text: Diana's crazy about people without clothes

indicators.note: being about something means surrounding it, so the slang word wraps the possessive

parts.note: nuts is slang for crazy
Di is the short form of Diana, so Diana's becomes Di's

explanation.surface: A woman named Diana who is wild about naturists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy about' reads as 'keen on', but splits into a word and a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudists choose to go naked, so they are people who wear nothing.

clue.text: Eurydice's husband composed her opus

indicators.note: something composed is put together, so the two words are arranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician writing a work for his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits the myth: the husband was the greatest musician of Greek legend, so composing an opus for her is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the musician Orpheus married Eurydice and went down to the underworld to bring her back.

clue.text: Calm policemen attached to port authority

parts.note: the PLA is the Port of London Authority, which runs the tidal Thames
the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the plain-clothes branch of British police

explanation.surface: Detectives seconded to the harbour board keeping things quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: Attached to puts the police after the authority, as a down clue hangs one under the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A placid person or sea is peaceful and undisturbed, which is what calm means.

clue.text: Soap bar is misshapen — there's a complaint about it

indicators.note: the illness goes around the jumbled letters just mentioned, enclosing them

parts.note: colic is a stomach ailment, and a complaint is an illness

indicators.note: something misshapen has lost its proper form, so these letters are bent into another order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling about a deformed bar of soap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' reads as a grumble but means an ailment. Carbolic soap is a red disinfectant soap once common in British homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbolic is a type of soap containing phenol, used as a disinfectant cleanser.

clue.text: Flags displayed by doctor above heart operations

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviated title for a doctor

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only its middle letter is kept

parts.note: the central letter of this five-letter word
ops is the common short form of operations

explanation.surface: A surgeon working above the heart, with flags on show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Above' does double duty in the surface as a position, but it is the word whose heart is taken. 'Flags' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to tire or wilt, and something that droops sags in the same way.

clue.text: A college window

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a college of Oxford University
second meaning: a bay window projecting from an upper storey

explanation.surface: Pointing out one particular window in a university building.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriel is one of the colleges of Oxford University, and an oriel is a projecting upper-floor bay window.

clue.text: Letters from people in books

definitions.meaning: first meaning: written symbols such as letters of an alphabet
second meaning: the figures in a novel or story

explanation.surface: Correspondence sent by figures from novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Typed or printed symbols are characters, and so are the fictional persons who appear in a novel.

clue.text: Date in Rome that is incomplete

indicators.note: incomplete means the phrase is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: id est is the Latin for 'that is', abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: An unfinished appointment in the Italian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin fits the Roman surface: drop the last letter of ID EST.
explanation.definitionFit: In the ancient Roman calendar the Ides fell in the middle of each month, the 15th or 13th.

clue.text: A military expedition caused trouble, with king being captured

indicators.note: something captured is held inside its captor, so the royal letter goes within
trouble here is the disorder the preceding word goes into, scrambling its letters

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An army campaign that made trouble and ended with a king taken prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caused trouble' reads as one phrase; split it, the second word scrambles the first.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crusades were medieval Christian military campaigns to the Holy Land, so a crusade is such a campaign.

clue.text: To reduce consumption is futile

parts.note: consumption is use of something
reducing means having less

explanation.surface: A cynic saying that cutting back on consumption is pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To reduce consumption' is the phrase 'use less' run together into one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something useless serves no purpose, and a futile effort likewise achieves nothing.
